title: Classes
summary: Describe a kind of object once with a class, then create many objects and extend it with inheritance.

quiz.q: Which keyword creates a new object from a class?
quiz.explain: `new Student('Asha')` runs the constructor and gives back a fresh object. The `class` keyword only defines the blueprint.
The constructor stores `'Tommy'` in `this.name`. Inside `speak`, `this` is that same object.

quiz.q: Click the line that makes `area()` return the wrong answer.
quiz.explain: Line 3 only assigns the parameter to itself. To store the value on the object you must write `this.size = size;`, otherwise `this.size` stays `undefined`.

quiz.q: Make `Topper` inherit from `Student` and call the parent constructor.
quiz.explain: `extends` links the child class to its parent. `super(...)` runs the parent constructor and must come before you use `this`.

quiz.q: Put the parts of a class in the usual order.
quiz.explain: A class holds the constructor first, then the methods. Methods are written without the word `function`.

exercise.task:
In `classes.js`, finish two classes:

- `Student` has a `constructor(name)` that stores `name` and an empty `marks` array. The method `addMark(mark)` pushes a mark. The method `average()` returns the average of the marks, or `0` when there are none. The method `describe()` returns `Name: average`, for example `Asha: 80`.
- `Topper` extends `Student`. Its `describe()` returns the parent's text followed by ` (topper)`, for example `Asha: 80 (topper)`. Use `super`.
hints: Inside methods, use `this.marks` and `this.name` to reach the data of the current object.
average() can add all marks with a loop or reduce, then divide by `this.marks.length`. In Topper, call `super.describe()` to get the parent's text.
